title: Freddie Keppard: early violin, trumpet lessons, Chicago
summary: Gabriel knew Freddie Keppard as a violinist who played with his father, took trumpet lessons, and went to Chicago in 1910.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: They call that the Cats and Jammer. That's right, Cats and Jammer. The Parkland Cocktails. That's nice. Well I was going to ask about Freddie Keppard, if you could tell a little bit more about him. You knew him when he first started then?
Well, on the air, I knew him before he was playing violin. He used to play violin with my daddy, Freddie. Freddie Keppard and Louis Keppard is around.

Yeah, he's still here. I know him quite well. Well, yeah. I never did get to meet his brother. I have some of his records, Freddie's records. Never met Louis? Oh, Louis, I know. But not Freddie. Freddie died before I got...

Well, Freddie went to Chicago, looking book 1910. He went to Chicago 1910. Him and my impressed never could get along together. So when I went... Do you know where he took lessons or what he did? With R.C. Bia. That's all I can tell you. R.C. Bia. Freddie Keppard took lessons from R.C. Bia on the trumpet. Now the violin, I couldn't tell you who taught him because I wouldn't know anything about that. But the trumpet, he took lessons from R.C. Bia on the... He was a top trumpet player too. Always could read the music. All he'd get to ping and then the rip and he was gone. So he made history on that trumpet in 1910. He went to Chicago. So that's the only man Benny Goodman talked about Freddie Keppard. He don't talk about Louis Armstrong, even Joe Alvon.
He was up there before then.
Yeah, he was ten years. The job was there in 1923.
See, that's when Louis Armstrong went there.
